scenarios.name: Hero Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays MirDB branding, tagline, and call-to-action buttons correctly

steps.description: Navigate to the MirDB homepage URL
steps.context: User lands on the page for the first time

steps.description: Check that the product name 'MirDB' is prominently displayed with the tagline about persistent key-value store with memcached compatibility
steps.context: Hero section should be visible without scrolling

steps.description: Confirm presence of 'Get Started' primary button and 'View on GitHub' secondary button
steps.context: CTAs should be clearly visible and styled appropriately

test_cases.input: Load homepage and inspect hero section
test_cases.expected: Product name 'MirDB' is visible in hero section
Tagline mentions 'persistent key-value store' and 'memcached compatibility'
'Get Started' button is present and clickable
'View on GitHub' button is present and links to external repository

scenarios.name: Key Features Section
scenarios.description: Verify the features section displays all key MirDB capabilities with clear descriptions

steps.description: Scroll to or click navigation to reach the features section
steps.context: Features section should be accessible from navigation

steps.description: Check that all key features are displayed as cards with icons, titles, and descriptions
steps.context: Expected features: Memcached Protocol Compatibility, Persistent Storage, LSM Tree Architecture, Async Networking

steps.description: Confirm each feature card has a brief, understandable description
steps.context: Descriptions should be concise and informative

test_cases.input: Check for Memcached Protocol Compatibility feature
test_cases.expected: Feature card exists with title and description about memcached protocol support
Feature card exists mentioning SSTables and durable storage

test_cases.input: Check for LSM Tree Architecture feature
test_cases.expected: Feature card exists explaining LSM tree design for write optimization
Feature card exists mentioning Tokio-based async networking
Each feature card has icon, title, and description arranged consistently

scenarios.name: Getting Started Section
scenarios.description: Verify the getting started section provides clear installation and usage instructions

steps.description: Scroll to or click navigation to reach the getting started section
steps.context: Section should be easily accessible

steps.description: Check for clear instructions on how to install/run MirDB
steps.context: Should include command examples

steps.description: Check for basic usage code examples with syntax highlighting
steps.context: Code should demonstrate connecting and performing operations

steps.description: Check for TOML configuration snippet showing basic config options
steps.context: Should show key configuration parameters

test_cases.expected: Installation/run instructions are visible with command examples
Code example shows how to connect using memcached client
Code snippets have proper syntax highlighting applied
TOML configuration example is displayed with key parameters
Default port 12333 is mentioned in getting started instructions

scenarios.name: Commands Reference Section
scenarios.description: Verify the commands section displays all supported memcached commands with descriptions

steps.description: Scroll to or click navigation to reach the commands section
steps.context: Section should list all supported commands

steps.description: Check that commands are organized by category: Storage, Retrieval, Deletion, Admin
steps.context: Clear categorization helps users understand available operations

steps.description: Check that each command has a name and behavior description
steps.context: Users need to understand what each command does

test_cases.expected: SET, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND commands are listed
GET, GETS commands are listed
DELETE command is listed
INFO, MAJOR_COMPACTION commands are listed
Each command has a brief description of its behavior

scenarios.name: Architecture Overview Section
scenarios.description: Verify the architecture section displays LSM tree diagram and data flow explanation

steps.description: Scroll to or click navigation to reach the architecture section
steps.context: Section should explain MirDB internals

steps.description: Check for visual SVG diagram showing LSM tree data flow
steps.context: Diagram should be clear and informative

steps.description: Check for explanation of write path: Request → WAL → Memtable → SSTs
steps.context: Users should understand how writes are handled

steps.description: Check for explanation of read path from memtable through SST levels
steps.context: Users should understand how reads are handled

test_cases.expected: SVG or image diagram of LSM tree architecture is displayed

test_cases.input: Verify diagram is an SVG element
test_cases.expected: Architecture diagram uses SVG format for scalability
Write path mentions WAL, Memtable, and SSTables
Read path explains lookup from memtable through SST levels

scenarios.name: Configuration Section
scenarios.description: Verify the configuration section displays default values and tunable parameters

steps.description: Scroll to or click navigation to reach the configuration section
steps.context: Section should help users configure MirDB

steps.description: Check that default configuration values are listed
steps.context: Port: 12333, Memtable size: 4MB, SSTable size: 100MB, LSM levels: 7

steps.description: Check that each parameter has a description of its purpose
steps.context: Users need to understand what each parameter controls

test_cases.expected: Default port 12333 is documented
Default memtable size 4MB is documented
Default SSTable size 100MB is documented
Default 7 LSM levels is documented
Configuration is shown in TOML format with proper syntax highlighting

steps.description: Check that navigation contains: Logo, Features, Getting Started, Documentation, GitHub links

steps.description: Click each internal anchor link and verify smooth scroll to section
steps.context: Navigation should scroll smoothly to target sections

steps.description: Verify GitHub link opens in new tab
steps.context: External links should have appropriate target attribute

test_cases.expected: Navigation bar is visible at top of page
Logo or 'MirDB' text is present in navigation
Page scrolls to features section

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Mobile
scenarios.description: Verify the homepage displays correctly on mobile devices (320px-480px viewport)

steps.description: Resize browser to 320px width to simulate mobile device
steps.context: Testing smallest supported viewport

steps.description: Check that all content is readable without horizontal scrolling
steps.context: Text should reflow to fit viewport

steps.description: Check that navigation collapses to mobile-friendly format (hamburger menu)
steps.context: Navigation should be accessible on small screens

steps.description: Check that images and diagrams scale appropriately
steps.context: Visual elements should fit viewport

test_cases.expected: No horizontal scrollbar appears, content fits viewport
Navigation shows mobile menu (hamburger) or stacked links
Hero content is readable and CTAs are tappable
Feature cards stack vertically and are fully visible
Code snippets have horizontal scroll or wrap appropriately

steps.description: Check that layout adapts appropriately for medium screens
steps.context: May show 2-column layouts for feature cards

steps.description: Check that interactive elements have adequate touch target size

test_cases.expected: Layout is optimized for tablet, no horizontal scroll
Feature cards show in 2-column grid or appropriate layout

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Desktop

test_cases.expected: Desktop layout is displayed with full navigation

test_cases.input: Check feature cards layout at desktop

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Semantic Structure
scenarios.description: Verify the page uses proper semantic HTML and heading hierarchy

steps.description: Analyze DOM for semantic HTML elements
steps.context: Should use header, nav, main, section, footer, etc.

steps.description: Check that headings follow proper hierarchy (h1 > h2 > h3)

steps.description: Verify presence of ARIA landmarks or semantic elements

test_cases.expected: Page has exactly one h1 element (MirDB)

Navigation is wrapped in nav element
Main content is wrapped in main element
Footer content is wrapped in footer element

scenarios.name: Accessibility - Color Contrast

steps.context: Non-text contrast requirements

test_cases.expected: Body text meets 4.5:1 contrast ratio against background
Headings meet 3:1 contrast ratio (large text) against background
Button text and borders meet contrast requirements
